$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §3 (coordinates), §4 (c14n/quanta), §5 (locators and typed absence), §6 (derivation), §9 (no confidence). Written from crates/ethos-parser-pdf/src/{extract,nodes}.rs. This is NOT DocumentRepresentation v0 — that envelope and the grounding projection land at M5.
title: Extract artifact (DRAFT)
description: Position-aware text runs whose origins are trustworthy, whose boxes are measured or typed-absent, and whose parse stopped rather than silently dropping content.

identity.description: artifact_type is `ethos.parser.extract.v0`, and schema_version is `EXTRACT_SCHEMA_VERSION` in crates/ethos-parser-pdf/src/extract.rs. Both DRAFT.

reading_order_rule.$comment: `gutter-columns-v2` since D4-S2 and `gutter-columns-v1` since v1-S5, which are one cut under two ids — the second reports the regions it made and the first discards them: runs are ordered by whitespace in page space, so a two-column document reads column-major and a page showing no gutter keeps content-stream order untouched. Nothing counts lines — pdf-inspector's rule flips on min_lines < 15, so a one-line edit reorders a whole page, and the two-column-14-lines/-15-lines fixture pair exists to hold this rule to the opposite. `single-column-v1` is v0's value and still legal: content-stream order with no reordering, which leaves a multi-column document visibly wrong and declares it.

pages.$comment: Per-page results for the PROCESSED pages only. A page missing from this list was not read, and `assurance.page_states` says which of the reasons applied — its absence here is never evidence that the page holds no text. A test asserts pages.length == coverage.pages_processed.

outlines.$comment: The catalog's /Outlines, as the representation carries them. Optional on the wire and always written: empty means the reader looked and the catalog named none, and `assurance.capabilities.outlines` says whether it looked.

assurance.$comment: The L1 gate (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §7): declared capabilities, limitations, per-page state, coverage, and terminal state. ABSORBS M3's `not_decoded` list, which no longer exists on the wire — absent font widths are now the document-scoped `font-widths-absent` limitation, and undescended form XObjects are declared twice on purpose: the profile-scoped `form-xobject-text-not-descended` states that this engine never descends, and the document-scoped `form-xobjects-not-descended` carries how many this document drew. It also carries the explicit multi-column reading-order limitation that synthetic/two-columns pins.

index.$comment: 1-based, as the document numbers its pages.

width.$comment: Integer centipoints, AFTER rotation: a quarter turn swaps the visible dimensions.

tables.$comment: Tables a geometric rule reconstructed on this page. The representation carries them as table records.

tagged_tables.$comment: Tables the structure tree declares that no geometric rule matched (v2-S24). Omitted when there are none.

figures.$comment: Figure regions `figure-regions-v1` found on this page (decision #46). Omitted when there are none. The representation carries them as figure records.

objects.$comment: Form fields and annotations (v1-S4): PDF objects, not glyph runs.

char_codes.$comment: NOT 1:1 with `text`. A ligature is one code and several scalars: the fi glyph is code 0x03 and characters f and i. The ligature-fi fixture produces 11 characters from 9 codes.

scalar_code_mismatch.$comment: True when text.chars().count() != char_codes.len(). DECLARED, not reconciled — reconciling means dropping one side or the other. LiteParse notes the same caveat in a doc comment; this puts it on the wire where a consumer can act on it.

synthesized.description: Characters this reader inserted. Empty for a run taken verbatim from the document.
synthesized.$comment: Generalises LiteParse's `trailing_space_generated`, the best honesty field in the four surveyed projects (checklist L6). A reader that inserts a character has authored content, and unflagged authored content is indistinguishable from evidence. Flagged AT CREATION, not reconstructed later.

font_size.$comment: Integer centipoints. NEVER used as a box height — pdf-inspector's TextItem.height is literally the same variable as font_size (checklist P5), which is why a separate measured geometry exists.

region.$comment: The representation's text_run.region: which region of its page the reading-order cut placed this run in. Written as null, not omitted, where the cut made no division.

block.$comment: The representation's text_run.block: which leading-gap block of its page this run is in. Null where the rule declined.

layout_unit.$comment: Decision #38, as on the representation's text_run. Absent where the rule gave the run no unit.

inferred_heading.$comment: Decision #29, as on the representation's text_run. Absent where false.

inferred_heading_level.$comment: Decision #38, as on the representation's text_run. Absent at level 1.

bold.$comment: Decision #38, as on the representation's text_run. Absent where false.

italic.$comment: Decision #38, as on the representation's text_run. Absent where false.

script.$comment: Decision #40, as on the representation's text_run. Absent on a run set on its line.

furniture.$comment: Decision #41, as on the representation's text_run. Absent on every line that is not page furniture.

mcid.$comment: Marked-content id, present only when the document supplies one via BDC. Omitted otherwise — never invented (Workbench rule 3).

structural.$comment: The representation's structural_locator for this run. Omitted when the page marked nothing.

findings.$comment: As on the representation's text_run. Omitted when empty.

quant_rect.$comment: A table or cell rectangle in integer centipoints, as the detector measured it. An object here, where the representation writes a QRect as [x0, y0, x1, y1].

rect.$comment: The union of the clustered paths' boxes, within the page, in page space.

tagged_check.$comment: Written as null, not omitted, where the structure tree describes no /Table on this page.

pdf_locator.title: NativeLocator, PDF variant
pdf_locator.description: Required on every run. Page plus baseline origin plus advance, in integer centipoints, in the declared top-left coordinate system after page rotation.
pdf_locator.$comment: The origin is the fingerprint-critical primitive: two independent PDF stacks agree on character origin to 0.001 pt while disagreeing on height by 6.174 pt. That asymmetry is why origins are identity and boxes are inspection.

advance.$comment: OMITTED, not zero, when the document carries no width information. A standard-14 font may legally omit /Widths and expect built-in AFM metrics, which this profile does not vendor — so the advance is unknown, and unknown is what it says. The origin is unaffected: it comes from the content stream, not from the font.
